REGULATIONS FOR THE RESTRICTION OF GUNS, CANNONS,
OR AMMUNITION USED FOR MILITARY PURPOSES.
(PROMULGATED OCTOBER 27TH, 1928.)

Article 1. Whoever, with intent to put to a criminal use,
manufactures, keeps, trafficks, smuggles or sells or buys
any gun, cannon, or ammunition used for military purposes,
shall be punished with imprisonment for not less than six
months and not more than five years.
Whoever, with intent to supply to another for
a criminal use, manufactures, keeps, trafficks, smuggles,
or sells or buys any gun, cannon, or ammunition used for
military purposes, shall be liable to the same punishment.
An attempt to commit any offence under this
article shall be punishable.

Article 2. Whoever, without authority or without being
able to give good reasons, manufactures, keeps, trafficks,
smuggles, or sells or buys any gun, cannon or ammunition
used for military purposes, shall be punished with impri-
sonment for not more than three years or detention or a
fine of not more than five hundred yuan.
An attempt to commit any offence under this
article shall be punishable.

Article 3. Whoever, being a police officer or other officer
whose duty it is to search and examine and knowing that
any person is committing the offences of the two preceding
articles, fails to take due measures concerning the matter
or conspires with the offenders, shall be punished with the
heaviest punishment under the said preceding articles.

Article 4. These regulations shall take effect from the date
of promulgation.

限制为军事目的使用的枪支、火炮或弹药的条例。
（1928年10月27日颁布。）

第一条. 凡意图用于犯罪目的，制造、保管、贩卖、走私或买卖任何用于军事目的的枪支、火炮或弹药者，处六个月以上五年以下有期徒刑。
凡意图供他人用于犯罪目的，制造、保管、贩卖、走私或买卖任何用于军事目的的枪支、火炮或弹药者，亦受同等处罚。
企图犯本条之罪者，应予处罚。

第二条. 凡未经授权或无法提出正当理由，制造、保管、贩卖、走私或买卖任何用于军事目的的枪支、火炮或弹药者，处三年以下有期徒刑、拘役或五百元以下罚金。
企图犯本条之罪者，应予处罚。

第三条. 凡警察官员或其他负有搜查和检查职责的官员，明知有人犯前两条之罪，而未对该事项采取适当措施，或与罪犯串通者，按前述各条中最重之刑罚处罚。

第四条. 本条例自颁布之日起生效。

THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, MARCH 17, 1929

Consul's Protest
Of Procedure Of
Search For Arms
Method Of Dealing With
Contrabands Criticised
By British

A letter is reported to have been sent to the Bureau of foreign Affairs by the British Consul-General in Shanghai, demanding that proper procedure should be adopted by the Chinese authorities in making searches on foreign vessels. The letter, it is learned, has been written as a result of the recent search made by the Detective Squad of the Garrison Commander's Headquarters aboard a British vessel, Tungting.

While the contents of the British Consul-General's letter have not been made known, it is generally presumed that the letter is in the form of a protest against the search which was made not in accordance with the usual and proper procedure. The Bureau of Foreign Affairs, however, has written to the Garrison Commander's Headquarters, enquiring about the actual circumstances in connection with the recent search aboard the s.s. Tungting.

Owing to frequent smuggling of contrabands, such as opium, arms and ammunitions, etc., aboard foreign vessels, however, the Chinese military and police authorities have thought it necessary to conduct searches or raids on any vessels aboard which are reported to carry contrabands, without first seeking sanction and co-operation from the Customs authorities. This procedure, which is against the usual practice, has been the subject of frequent complaints from the foreign authorities concerned.

The Chinese authorities, however, hold the opinion that such necessity of urgency cannot be compared with the common matters which only require usual treatment.

据报道，英国驻上海总领事已向外交部致函，要求中国当局在对外国船只进行搜查时采用适当的程序。据悉，这封信是因卫戍司令部侦探队最近在英国船只“洞庭”号上进行的搜查而写的。

虽然英国总领事信函的内容尚未公开，但人们普遍推测，该信函是以抗议形式提出的，反对此次未按通常和适当程序进行的搜查。然而，外交部已致函卫戍司令部，询问最近在“洞庭”号轮船上进行搜查的有关实际情况。

由于外国船只上经常走私鸦片、武器和弹药等违禁品，中国军警当局认为有必要对任何被报告载有违禁品的船只进行搜查或突击检查，而无需事先寻求海关当局的批准和合作。这种违反惯例的程序一直是相关外国当局频繁投诉的主题。

然而，中国当局认为，这种紧急必要性不能与只需按常规处理的普通事务相提并论。

THE CHINA WEEKLY REVIEW February 23, 1929.
ABOLISHING SOMETHING WHICH
NEVER EXISTED
SECRETARY of State Kellogg in a statement
before the Foreign Relations Committee of the
House of Representatives at Washington on
Monday of this week said that all of the countries
which had placed embargoes on the shipment of arms
to China, “were now considering lifting them.” One
wonders if Mr. Kellogg could have been serious when
he made that statement, because of all of the interna-
tional farces which have been staged in recent times
the China arms embargo has been the most farcical.
The question of placing an embargo on the shipment
of arms to China was first raised by the American
Minister, Dr. Paul Reinsch in Peiping about the year
1918. According to a report on the subject which
was made at the Washington Conference, the British
Government agreed to the American proposal, but the
Italian Minister while agreeing in principle, made a
reservation regarding “certain unfulfilled contracts for
arms which certain Italian subjects had negotiated
with the Chinese.” What the Italian Minister had
in mind was a shipment of arms and ammunition at
that time stored in the Italian Concession in Tientsin,
the value of which was estimated at $5,000,000. After
receiving bids from both sides in the Chinese civil
war the Italians finally sold their stock of arms to the
Chihli faction. In view of the refusal of the Italians
to agree to the embargo proposed by Dr. Reinsch the
Japanese and one or two other ministers also made
reservations so that the whole thing went by the boards.
The subject was again brought up at the Washington
Conference in 1921-1922 when Secretary Hughes,
apparently with the approval of the British Delega-
tion proposed a resolution placing a definite embargo
on the shipment of arms to China. The Italians
again made a reservation regarding “unfilled con-
tracts” which brought forth a caustic remark from
Mr. Balfour, head of the British Delegation. But
the Italian reservation stuck and was immediately
followed by similar reservations again by the Japan-
ese, Belgians, Dutch, and so on, the general result of
which was the throwing out of the resolution entirely.
Immediately following the Washington Conference
President Harding secured the passage of a resolu-
tion through Congress placing a heavy penalty on
anyone exporting American arms to China, but
neglecting to make it a crime for American citizens
to deal in arms outside of the United States. The
British Government also passed a similar law, but
even though the American and British regulations
were effective in preventing direct arms exports
from America and England to China, the regulations
had little effect because neither Germany nor Russia
were bound and these two nations were completely
free to sell all the arms they could get the Chinese to
pay for. Then in addition to the arms situation there
was the matter of airplanes for military use, both
the French and Italians doing their best in this field,
while the Japanese made hay in Manchuria by selling
arms, munitions, field artillery and airplanes in the
bargain. About the only effect which the American
and British arms embargoes have had has been to
keep Americans and Britons out of a profitable
business which has been participated in by the
nationals of about every country on the face of the
globe. In view of this situation we can’t help but
feel that Mr. Kellogg must have been joking when
he spoke of lifting the China arms embargo!
（批：I am of the same opinion. JLB）

废除从未存在过的事物

国务卿凯洛格（Kellogg）本周星期一在华盛顿向众议院外交关系委员会发表声明称，所有对向中国运输武器实施禁运的国家，“目前正考虑解除禁运”。人们不禁怀疑，凯洛格先生发表该声明时是否认真，因为在近期上演的所有国际闹剧中，对华武器禁运可谓最为荒诞不经。

关于对中国实施武器运输禁运的问题，最初是由美国驻华公使芮恩施博士（Dr. Paul Reinsch）于1918年左右在北平提出的。根据华盛顿会议上就此问题所作的一份报告，英国政府同意了美国的提议，但意大利公使虽然在原则上表示同意，却就“某些意大利臣民与中方商谈的某些未履行的武器合同”提出了保留意见。意大利公使所指涉的，是当时储存在天津意租界的一批军火弹药，其估值约为500万美元。在收到中国内战双方的出价后，意大利人最终将其库存武器卖给了直系军阀。鉴于意大利人拒绝同意芮恩施博士提出的禁运方案，日本公使及其他一两位公使也提出了保留意见，致使整个计划彻底搁浅。

1921-1922年华盛顿会议期间，该议题再次被提出。当时，休斯国务卿（Secretary Hughes）显然在英国代表团的支持下，提出了一项决议，旨在对向中国运输武器实施明确的禁运。意大利人再次就“未履行之合同”提出保留意见，此举引来了英国代表团团长贝尔福先生（Mr. Balfour）的一句尖刻评论。然而，意大利的保留意见得以坚持，并随即引发了日本、比利时、荷兰等国代表类似的保留意见，其总体结果导致该决议被完全否决。

华盛顿会议结束后不久，哈定总统促使国会通过了一项决议，对任何向美国境外出口武器至中国的行为处以重罚，但却疏忽了将美国公民在美国境外从事武器交易定为犯罪这一条款。英国政府也通过了类似的法律，但是，尽管美英两国的法规有效阻止了从美国和英国直接向中国出口武器，但这些法规收效甚微，因为德国和俄罗斯并不受其约束，这两个国家完全可以自由地向中国人出售任何他们愿意付款购买的武器。此外，除了武器局势外，还有军用飞机的问题，法国和意大利在此领域极力推销，而日本则通过在满洲出售武器、弹药、野战炮以及搭售飞机而大发横财。美英武器禁运产生的唯一影响，大概就是将美国人和英国人排除在一项利润丰厚的生意之外，而这项生意几乎有全球各国的国民参与。鉴于此种情况，我们不禁觉得，当凯洛格先生谈及解除对华武器禁运时，一定是在开玩笑！
（批注：我持相同观点。JLB）
（批注：美国海军情报。JLB 1929年2月27日。）
（批注：a. e. (政治处) 谁 1929年2月27日。）

PEKING & TIENTSIN TIMES, WEDNESDAY, FEBRUARY 20, 1929.

THE ARMS EMBARGO.

A CABLE which we print this morning confirms the report that the American Government is about to cancel the Arms Embargo against China at an early date. The Secretary of State has made a statement to this effect to the House Military Affairs Committee, and it is construed, in Washington, as an additional manifestation of the belief that the Nationalist Government is firm, and that allowing shipments of arms to China will not be an incentive to fresh civil warfare. This is the interpretation that would naturally be placed upon the American Government's decision in political circles. Actually, however, the State Department is probably actuated as much by the futility of the embargo, as by any faith in the stability of the Nationalist Government, or any belief that the importation of arms will not act as an incentive to civil war. The plain truth is that the Embargo, from the date it was first enforced, nearly ten years ago, has been a complete fiasco. It was never adhered to by several States which were in a position to export arms of their own or other countries' manufacture, and it was so vaguely phrased that bonafide foreign traders were in genuine doubt as to the extent of the prohibition.
The proposal of an Arms Embargo was first made by the American Minister at Peking on April 8, 1919. During the following month there was an exchange of views between the major Powers, and on May 5 a Note was communicated to the Waichiaopu announcing that the Governments of Great Britain, Spain, Portugal, the United States, Russia, Brazil, France and Japan had "agreed effectively to restrain their subjects and citizens from exporting to or importing into, China arms and munitions of war, and materials destined exclusively for their manufacture until the establishment of a Government whose authority is recognized throughout the whole country, and also to prohibit during the above period the delivery of arms and munitions for which contracts have already been made but not executed." The Representatives of the Netherlands, Denmark, Belgium, and Italy were stated to be in full accord with this

THE KING.
A QUIET DAY.

London, Feb. 18.
"The King in much better and cheerful mood." These were the words of the Queen replying to an inquiry regarding the King's progress when she visited the exhibition of English decorative art in London to-day.
Her Majesty had come to the town for the first time since the King was taken to Bognor nine days ago. She was warmly embraced by a number of her friends when she arrived at the exhibition hall and it was believed by all present that the welcome, which they extended to her, was the first she had received, on a purely social occasion, since the King's illness.

London, Feb. 18.
It is officially stated at Craigwell House this evening that the King has passed a quiet day. A cold easterly wind blew throughout the day, but there was some sunshine during the afternoon, and the King took the advantage of this and sat by the window for some time.

LARGE ORDER BY GERMANY FOR THE BRITISH INDUSTRIAL FAIR.

London, Feb. 18
An order for honey worth £9,000 was placed early in the day by Germany for Medical purposes. A remarkable point about these Dominion exhibits is the cleverness of scenic arrangements obtained by paintings and grouping of fruit and other things. The Queen will be accompanied by the Prince of Wales when she visits tomorrow Birmingham, or the heavy section of the Fair was opened by the Lord Mayor of Birmingham. At a subsequent luncheon, Mr Amery, Secretary for the Dominions, said the Fair continued to make headway and was fulfilling its national use. The fact the British manufacturers had survived so difficult a period as they have was, he believed, bound to bring about great accession of strength.

武器禁运。

今晨刊登的一条电报证实了如下报道：美国政府即将在近期取消对华武器禁运。国务卿已向众议院军事事务委员会发表了以此为宗旨的声明，在华盛顿，这被解读为一种额外的表现，表明美方相信国民政府立场坚定，且允许向中國运输武器不会成为引发新一轮内战的诱因。这是政治圈对美国政府决定自然产生的解读。然而实际上，国务院采取此举，可能是出于对禁运无效性的考量，其程度不亚于其对国民政府稳定性的信心，或其认为武器进口不会助长内战的信念。事实真相是，禁运自近十年前首次实施之日起，便是一场彻底的失败。几个有能力出口本国或他国制造武器的国家从未遵守该禁运，且其措辞如此模糊，以致诚信的外国商人对禁令的范围确实感到疑惑。

提出武器禁运的建议，最初由美国驻北平公使于1919年4月8日提出。在接下来的一个月里，主要列强之间交换了意见，并于5月5日向外交部（Waichiaopu）递交了一份照会，宣布大不列颠、西班牙、葡萄牙、美国、俄罗斯、巴西、法国和日本政府已“同意切实约束其臣民和公民，在全国性权威政府建立之前，不得向中国出口或从中国进口武器、军火及专用于制造上述物品的材料，并在上述期间禁止交付已签订但未执行的武器和军火合同”。据悉，荷兰、丹麦、比利时和意大利的代表完全赞同此点

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C.I.D REGISTRY
February 28, 1929. No. C. 8760
Date.... K. 3. 29

SECRET & CONFIDENTIAL

The report of the seizure of the arms on board the S.S.
"Ouderkerk", as described in the "China Press" of February 23rd
contains several discrepancies.
The amount of arms and rounds of ammunition given in my
report dated February 22nd were actually seized by the Customs
search party and not by the Chinese River Police.
The exact amount of arms seized by the Chinese River Police
is not known to the Customs Authorities and the latter never
received any arms or ammunition from the Chinese River Police.
It is alleged, however, that the Chinese River Police seized
some 540 revolvers but surrendered only 40 of them to their own
people.
The Customs Authorities did not possess any actual information
regarding the place of concealment of the arms and the chief of
the search gang in this particular case was a fresh man.
The first search of the ship by the Customs before tiffin led
to the discovery of one pistol, one revolver and 148 rounds of
ammunition.
When the search party stopped at the water tank and gave
instructions to have it opened, they were told it contained the
only supply of fresh water the ship contained and that there was
no other tank into which it could be pumped. The search was
resumed after tiffin.
In the meantime the Chinese River Police sought out one of the
ship's firemen - a Chinese and were told the exact place of
concealment, namely, the water tank.
The Chinese River Police are not entitled to board the
steamers, but the chief officer gave them permission to search
the ship. They proceeded straight to the water tank, had the
water pumped out and discovered the arms. If they actually
seized the amount reported in the "China Press" of February 23rd,
which amount coincides with that seized by the Customs search
party, the water tank, which contains two divisions, must have
had two lots, for the after tiffin search made by the Customs
search gang led to the discovery of 194 Mausers, one automatic,
and 19552 rounds of ammunition in the said tank.
The Dutch shipping company has written to the Customs
asking why the Chinese River Police boarded their steamer
"Ouderkerk".

Ref. No. d/C.3.29.
Copy forwarded to H.B.M. Consul for information.
Lt. Col. G.H.R. Holland, C.B.E.
Capt. J.P. Shelley.
Lieut E.F. Carlson.

刑事侦缉处登记室
1929年2月28日。编号 C. 8760
日期.... K. 3. 29

秘密且机密

2月23日《字林西报》（China Press）所描述的关于“奥德克克”号（S.S. "Ouderkerk"）轮船上查获武器的报告，存在几处出入。
我在2月22日的报告中提到的武器和子弹数量，实际上是由海关搜查队查获的，而非由中国水警查获。
海关当局并不知晓中国水警查获的确切武器数量，且后者从未从中国水警那里接收过任何武器或弹药。
然而，据称中国水警查获了约540支左轮手枪，但仅向其上级上交了其中的40支。
海关当局并不掌握关于武器藏匿地点的任何实际信息，且在此特定案件中，搜查组的负责人是一名新人。
海关在午餐前对该船进行的第一次搜查，发现了一支手枪、一支左轮手枪和148发子弹。
当搜查组停在水箱旁并指示打开水箱时，他们被告知里面装有船上唯一的淡水供应，且没有其他水箱可以泵入这些水。搜查在午餐后恢复。
与此同时，中国水警找到了一名船上的中国司炉工，并获知了确切的藏匿地点，即水箱。
中国水警无权登上轮船，但大副允许他们搜查船只。他们径直前往水箱，将水抽出后发现了武器。如果他们确实查获了2月23日《字林西报》所报道的数量——该数量与海关搜查队查获的数量一致——那么，由于该水箱分为两个隔间，必定有两批货物，因为海关搜查队在午餐后的搜查中，在该水箱内发现了194支毛瑟枪、1支自动手枪和19,552发子弹。
这家荷兰航运公司已致函海关，询问中国水警为何登上他们的“奥德克克”号轮船。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, FRIDAY, MARCH 15, 1929

THE ARMS SEIZURE
ON THE OUDEKERK

Exchange of Letters Between
Dutch and Local Chinese
Authorities

The arms seizure aboard the
Dutch str. Oudekerk, several weeks
ago, has resulted in the exchange
of letters by Dutch Consul-General,
and the Commissioner of Foreign
Affairs.

The Dutch Consul-General (ac-
cording to the Chinese press) ad-
dressed a letter to the Foreign
Commissioner pointing out that the
steps taken by the Water Police
in seizing the arms were inadequate
in that the seizure should have been
made by the Customs.

In reply, Mr. Wunsz King stated
that the smuggling of arms was
totally different from the smuggling
of other contraband. The Water
Police had to search the vessel
without delay as there was a pos-
sibility of her leaving Shanghai.
The search was, therefore, made on
February 20. Furthermore, before
the search was carried out, says
the Foreign Commissioner, the
captain of the vessel had signed on
his permit the fact that the search
was carried out by the Water Police.
Therefore, he states, the Bureau of
Public Safety considered that the
steps taken were both necessary
and adequate.

Continuing, the Foreign Commis-
sioner said that he supported the
steps taken by the Bureau of Public
Safety in the matter because it was
most alarming to learn that a
Dutch vessel should smuggle such
a large consignment of munitions
—300 pistols and 20,000 rounds of
ammunition. Were it not for the
proper precautions of the Water
Police, he continued, these would
have fallen into the hands of evil
characters and the lives and pro-
perty of law-abiding citizens would
be menaced.

In further support of his reply,

Mr. King drew attention to the fact
that the munitions were carefully
and cleverly concealed in different
parts of the ship, from which he
inferred that the vessel had been
engaged in arms smuggling on more
than one occasion.

Concluding, the Foreign Commis-
sioner requested the Dutch Consul-
General to punish the persons re-
sponsible, as well as the smugglers,
in order that the law would be up-
held and friendly relations between
the Netherlands and China main-
tained.

《字林西报》，1929年3月15日，星期五

奥德凯克号（Oudekerk）军火查获案

荷兰当局与中国地方当局之间的信函往来

数周前在荷兰籍轮船“奥德凯克”号（str. Oudekerk）上查获军火一事，已导致荷兰总领事与外交专员之间互换信函。

据中文报刊报道，荷兰总领事致函外交专员，指出水上警察在查获军火时采取的措施不足，认为该项查获本应由海关进行。

作为回复，金问政先生（Mr. Wunsz King）表示，军火走私与其他违禁品走私截然不同。由于该船有可能离开上海，水上警察必须立即对该船进行搜查。因此，搜查于2月20日进行。此外，外交专员称，在实施搜查之前，船长已在许可证上签署确认搜查由水上警察执行。因此，他表示，公安局认为所采取的措施既必要又充分。

外交专员接着表示，他支持公安局在此事上采取的措施，因为获悉一艘荷兰船只竟走私如此大批军火——300支手枪和20,000发子弹——令人极为震惊。他继续说道，若非水上警察采取了适当的预防措施，这些军火就会落入不法分子之手，守法公民的生命财产将受到威胁。

为了进一步支持其回复，

金先生提请注意这样一个事实：军火被仔细且巧妙地隐藏在船上的不同部位，由此他推断该船不止一次从事军火走私活动。

最后，外交专员请荷兰总领事惩处责任人以及走私者，以维护法律尊严并保持荷兰与中国之间的友好关系。

When the search party stopped at
water trunk and gave instructions
to have it opened, they were told it
contained the only supply of fresh water
the ship contained and that there was
no other tank into which it could
be pumped. The search was resumed
after tiffin.

In the meantime the Chinese
River Police caught one of the ship's
firemen - a Chinese (whom they
tortured into confessing the whereabouts
of the arms) and were told the exact
place of concealment, namely the
water tank.

The Chinese River Police are not
entitled to board the steamers, but
they scared the Chief Officer into giving
them permission to search the ship.
They proceeded straight to the water

discovered the arms. If they actually

The Dutch shipping company has written to the

boarded their steamer "Ouderkerk".

中国水上警察无权登上轮船，但他们恐吓大副，迫使其允许他们搜查船只。他们径直前往水箱，将水抽出，从而发现了军火。如果他们确实查获了2月23日《大陆报》报道的数量（该数量与海关搜查队查获的数量一致），那么分为两部分的水箱内必然有两批军火，因为海关搜查组在午餐后的搜查中，在该水箱内发现了184支毛瑟枪、7支自动手枪和19,552发子弹。

THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, FEBRUARY 22, 1930.

Large Seizure Of Arms Reported In Chinese Papers
Chinese River Police Effect Raid On Dutch Ship

The seizure of 186 revolvers and about 20,000 rounds of ammunition by the River Police of the Public Safety Bureau of the Greater Shanghai Municipality, as a result of a raid on a Dutch steamer in port, was prominently reported in yesterday's Chinese press.

The Dutch steamer in question is said to be the s.s. Ouderkerk which steamed in to Shanghai harbor on the 18th instant and anchored off Mackenzie and Co.'s Pootung godown. According to a report to the Chinese River Police, delivery of a big consignment of arms was expected to be made the same night. A squad of Chinese police, headed by Capt. W. H. Li, was immediately sent in two launches to keep a close watch on the movements of the Ouderkerk, the raiding party hiding themselves in the dark in a remote corner.

Up to 4 a.m. on the 20th, nothing occurred and a portion of the police returned to their camp. At about noon on the 20th, it is alleged, a further report was received by the Police that the ship would sail from Shanghai the same afternoon without delivering the arms on board. Col. K. K. Ho, Chief of the Chinese River Police, then led a squad of police and went aboard the ship to make a search. It was after repeated arguments with the ship's captain and other officials (all foreigners) that the searching squad were allowed to go aboard ship.

It was stated that the Customs officials had also received reports of arms smuggling but a search on the 19th failed to uncover anything on board the ship. The report to the Chinese River Police was in greater detail, and though the exact spot where the arms were concealed was not known, a general description of the ship was furnished by the informer.

The ship's four decks were thoroughly searched by the Chinese police. The arms, it is reported were not discovered until the raiders got to the very bottom where a small hole on a plate was first noticed. The total consignment of arms, reported to have been shipped from Europe, is alleged to have consisted of 186 revolvers of different types and 19,522 rounds of ammunition, and were all seized and conveyed to the Customs godown for safe custody pending further investigations.

According to a written view issued by the Chinese Customs Outdoor Staff's Club, the consignment of arms was stated to have been shipped originally from Hamburg and all the arms were of German make. Owing to a close watch by the Customs officials, there was no chance of delivering the contraband in Shanghai and the ship is said to have intended to sail for Hongkong on Thursday the 21st), when a seizure was made. The fact that the ship was allowed by Customs foreign officials to sail from Shanghai after the seizure was certainly illegal, says the Club, and due responsibility for negligence should be assumed by the Customs authorities. In conclusion, the Club urges the Chinese Government to cable to the Chinese Navy immediately to seize the ship, which should be confiscated. The ship's crew must also be placed under arrest for their being suspected of having a connection with the smuggling of the big consignment of arms, states the Club.

中文报纸报道大规模军火查获案
中国水上警察突袭荷兰船只

上海特别市公安局水上警察因突袭港内一艘荷兰轮船，查获186支左轮手枪和约20,000发子弹，此事在昨日的中文报纸上被显著报道。

据悉，涉事荷兰轮船为“奥德凯克”号（s.s. Ouderkerk），该船于本月18日驶入上海港，停泊在马根洋行（Mackenzie and Co.）浦东仓库外。据向中国水上警察举报的情报，预计当晚将交付大批军火。一队由李华（Capt. W. H. Li，音译）队长率领的中国警察立即乘坐两艘快艇出发，严密监视“奥德凯克”号的动向，突击队员隐蔽在远处黑暗的角落。

直到20日凌晨4点，未发生任何情况，部分警察返回营地。据称，20日中午左右，警方收到进一步报告，称该船将在当天下午不交付船上军火的情况下驶离上海。中国水上警察局长何侃（Col. K. K. Ho，音译）随即率领一队警察登船搜查。在与船长及其他官员（均为外国人）反复争论后，搜查队才被允许登船。

据说海关官员也收到了关于军火走私的报告，但19日的搜查未在船上发现任何东西。向中国水上警察提供的报告更为详细，虽然举报人不知道军火藏匿的确切位置，但提供了该船的大致描述。

中国警察彻底搜查了船的四个甲板。据报道，直到突击队员到达最底层，首先注意到钢板上的一个小洞时，才发现了军火。据报这批从欧洲运来的军火总数包括186支不同类型的左轮手枪和19,522发子弹，全部被查获并运至海关仓库妥善保管，以待进一步调查。

根据中国海关外勤职员俱乐部发表的一份书面意见，这批军火最初据称是从汉堡装运的，所有军火均为德国制造。由于海关官员的严密监视，这批违禁品没有机会在上海交付，据说该船原定于21日（星期四）驶往香港，此时进行了查获。该俱乐部称，海关外籍官员在查获后允许该船驶离上海显然是非法的，海关当局应承担疏忽的责任。最后，该俱乐部敦促中国政府立即致电中国海军扣押该船，并予以没收。该俱乐部称，船员也必须被捕，因为他们涉嫌与这批大宗军火走私有关。

THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, FEBRUARY 24, 1929.

Cannot Detain S. S. Ouderkerk,
Official Tells Local Newspaper

In connection with the seizure of a big quantity of arms from the Dutch steamer Ouderkerk, a representative of "San Wan Pao" called on Mr. W. R. Myers, Deputy Commissioner of the Shanghai Customs, on Friday to make further enquiries.

Below is a translation of what Mr. Myers was reported to have said in response to the representative's questions during the interview:

The interviewer first enquired whether there was any truth in the report that the foreign vessel, which carried a big consignment of arms, had been allowed to have sailed for Hongkong instead of being detained. Mr. Myers, after talking to the Harbor Master over the telephone, answered that the vessel had left Shanghai but would return to this port again before long.

Question: "When the vessel comes to Shanghai next time, what will the Shanghai Customs do with her,—to detain her or allow her free from legal treatment?"

Answer: "In order to avoid further smuggling, a thorough inspection will be made when the vessel comes again, but we cannot detain her. The duty of the Customs is inspection. Moreover, those who are responsible for smuggling the arms have all escaped and are untraceable."

Question: "Usually, the Shanghai Customs have the right to detain any vessel that is plague-infected; how is it that the Customs would allow the arms-smuggling vessel freedom?"

Answer: "The Customs can instruct plague-infected vessels to suspend sailings and not to place them under detention. As to arm-smuggling vessels, the Customs could detain them only by order of the Government."

Question: "Was any report submitted to the authorities after the seizure of the arms?"

Answer: "Yes, we submitted the report, but the authorities had already received information about it."

Question: "What will be done to the seized arms which are now stored in the Customs godown?"

Answer: "We are awaiting instructions from the Government as to what to do with same."

Mr. Myers also said that, according to his opinion, the seized arms were privately shipped here by the firemen of the vessel, and the vessel itself had nothing to do with the matter. Therefore, Mr. Myers said, the detention of the vessel was hardly possible.

官方人士告知本地报纸：无法扣留“奥德凯克”号轮船

就荷兰轮船“奥德凯克”号被查获大量军火一事，《三万报》（San Wan Pao，音译）代表于周五拜访上海海关副税务司迈尔斯先生（Mr. W. R. Myers），以作进一步查询。

以下是据报道迈尔斯先生在面谈中回答代表提问时的谈话译文：

采访者首先询问，有报道称载有大批军火的外国船只未被扣留，反而被允许驶往香港，此消息是否属实。迈尔斯先生通过电话与港务长交谈后回答说，该船已离开上海，但不久后将返回本港。

问：“下次该船来到上海时，上海海关将如何处置——是扣留它，还是允许其免受法律制裁？”

答：“为了避免进一步走私，当该船再次到来时将进行彻底检查，但我们不能扣留它。海关的职责是检查。此外，负责走私军火的人均已逃脱，无法追踪。”

问：“通常，上海海关有权扣留任何感染瘟疫的船只；为何海关会给予走私军火的船只自由？”

答：“海关可以指令感染瘟疫的船只暂停航行，而不是将其拘留。至于走私军火的船只，海关只有根据政府命令才能扣留它们。”

问：“查获军火后是否向当局提交了报告？”

答：“是的，我们提交了报告，但当局已经收到了相关信息。”

问：“目前存放在海关仓库的被查扣军火将如何处理？”

答：“我们正在等待政府关于如何处理这些军火的指示。”

迈尔斯先生还表示，在他看来，被查扣的军火是由该船司炉工私自运至此地的，船只本身与此事无关。因此，迈尔斯先生说，扣留该船几乎是不可能的。

亲爱的罗伯逊先生：

前次我曾向您提及，1928年3月31日颁布的关于德国公民向中国运输武器的德国法律，并非涵盖所有种类的武器，而仅涵盖那些根据《凡尔赛条约》禁止在德国制造的武器和弹药。

摆在我们面前的问题是对上述法律第1条中所载词语的解释，即：
1. 战争物资和战争弹药
2. 战争物资或战争弹药的主要部件

关于第1点。《凡尔赛条约》已成为德国法律的一部分，因此构成了对“战争物资”和“战争弹药”这两个词进行解释的基础，因为根据该条约，此类物品的进出口以及在德国的制造均被禁止。究竟什么是战争物资和战争弹药，该条约部分地作了定义，但此后在上述条约签署国之间进行了许多讨论，直到1927年7月27日的《战争物资法》由德国颁

I am enclosing a copy of the first 4 articles of the
said Law, which alone are essential. The same specify
exactly which war material and war ammunition come under
the Law. War material or war ammunition which is not
contained in the said Law, is also open for importation
to China and not subject to the Law of March 31st, 1928.
You will observe that Art. 3 para. 6 speaks of pistols
and revolvers and mentions that the calibre must exceed
8 mm. and the length of the barrel must be over 9.8 cm.
Smaller pistols could, therefore, be imported. This is
only an example, and with regard to other arms the Law will
have to be consulted before a decision could be made as to
whether such arms are permitted for importation or not.

Ad. 2. The interpretation of the words "essential parts"
has to be looked for in commentaries to other laws where
the expression "essential" is used. There might be a
decision of the German Supreme Court, giving an official
interpretation, but I do not have the same at my disposal.

My opinion is that as "essential parts" can be
considered only such parts which could be used at once
for the assembling of arms or ammunition without any further
process of manufacture. Essential parts would be half-
manufactures. A chemical unless contained in the Law of

兹附上该法前4条的副本，仅有这几条是至关重要的。这些条款确切规定了哪些战争物资和战争弹药受该法管辖。未包含在该法中的战争物资或战争弹药，也可以进口到中国，且不受1928年3月31日法律的约束。

您会注意到，第3条第6款提到了手枪和左轮手枪，并指出其口径必须超过8毫米，枪管长度必须超过9.8厘米。因此，较小口径的手枪可以进口。这只是一个例子，至于其他武器，在决定此类武器是否允许进口之前，必须查阅该法律。

关于第2点。“主要部件”一词的解释，需在其他使用“主要”(essential) 这一表述的法律注释中寻找。德国最高法院可能有一项判决对此给出了官方解释，但我手头没有该判决。

我认为，只有那些无需进一步制造过程即可立即用于组装武器或弹药的部件，才能被视为“主要部件”。主要部件将是半成品。除非包含在1927年7月27日的法律中，否则用于制造火药的化学品不能被视为主要部件。其他的例子包括步枪用钢、铜等。

相信本意见书能为您提供所有必要的解释，

谨致最诚挚的问候，

您真诚的，

1927 Issued in Berlin on August 5, 1928 No. 36.
Law Governing Munition
of War, July 27, 1927.

The Reichstag has decided upon the following
law, which is being made public with the permission of
the Government Council.

1.
The Export and Import of arms for war purposes
(arms, ammunition and other supplies) as well as the
manufacture of same for export purposes is prohibited.

2.
Munitions of War for inland use must not be
used, manufactured, stored or traded in the following:

3.
The following articles are covered by paragraphs
1 & 2, unless paragraph 7 stipulates something else.
1. Guns and Mine-throwers of every description as
well as their carriages and accessories .
2. Shells & Ammunition for the use of arms under
para. 1.
3. a) Ordnance of every description of all
calibres, together with their carriages.
b) Means of transportation & accessories for
these arms.
4. a) Arms, Bayonets & Carbines of all model,
which are used or will be used in the
arming of an army of some country, or-
b) Ammunition which is used by the German
German armed forces, or-
c) is not in use any longer in the defence of
a country, but still is good for war
purposes and destined for that use.
5. Shells & ammunition for the arms mentioned
under 3a and 4.
6. Pistols and Revolvers, Automatic or with self-
loading devices, with a barrel length of 9.8 cm.
or a cal. over 8 mm.
7. Contrivances for war purposes & machines for
the firing or throwing of bombs, torpedoes,
mines & other projectiles.
8. Hand, rifle & throwing grenades.
9. a) Land mines.
b) Bombs for war purposes.
10. Torpedo tubes and all mechanical devices for
for torpedoing.
11. a) Torpedo shells.
b) Torpedoes and their accessories.
12. Water bombs, towing explosive projectiles,
driving mines, and anchor sea-mines.
13. Munition cases and for the transport and storage
of war materials especially suitable packing
cases.
14. U. Boats & their optical tubes and special
equipment.
15. Substructures as well as mechanical contrivances
for marine artillery.

Abschrift
Reichsgesetzblatt
I. Teil
1927 ausgegeben zu BERLIN, den 5. August 1927. Nr36

Gesetz über Kriegsgerät.
Vom 27. Juli 1927.

Der Reichstag hat das folgende Gesetz beschlossen, das mit
Zustimmung des Reichsrats hiermit verkündet wird:

§ 1
Die Ein- und Ausfuhr von Kriegsgerät jeder Art (Waffen, Munition
und sonstigem Gerät) sowie seine Herstellung für die Ausfuhr ist
verboten.

§ 2
Kriegsgerät darf für inländische Verwendung weder hergestellt
noch aufbewahrt oder gehandelt werden.

§ 3
Unter die Vorschriften der §§ 1 und 2 fallen, soweit nicht
der § 7 etwas anderes bestimmt, folgende Erzeugnisse:
1. Geschütze und Minenwerfer jeder Art sowie deren Rohrswagen
und Lafetten; Sonderzubehör.
2. Geschosse und Munition für die in Ziffer 1 aufgeführten
Waffen.
3. a) Maschinenwaffen jeder Art und aller Kaliber sowie deren
Lafetten,
b) Transportmittel und Sonderzubehör für diese Waffen.
4. Gewehre, Stutzen und Karabiner aller Modelle, die
a) zur Bewaffnung der Wehrmacht irgendeines Staates ge-
hören oder gehören werden, oder
b) für die Verwendung einer in der deutschen Wehrmacht
eingeführten Munition eingerichtet sind, oder
c) nicht mehr zur Bewaffnung der Wehrmacht irgendeines
Staates gehören, aber noch für militärische Verwendung
in Frage kommen und für Kriegszwecke bestimmt sind.
5. Geschosse und Munition für die in den Ziffern 3a und 4
aufgeführten Waffen.
6. Pistolen und Revolver, automatisch oder mit Selbstladevor-
richtung, mit einer Lauflänge über 9,8 cm oder mit einem
Kaliber über 8 mm/
7. Für Kriegszwecke bestimmte Vorrichtungen und Maschinen für
das Ab schiessen oder Abwerfen von Bomben, Torpedos, Wasser bom-
ben und anderen Arten von Geschossen.

1927年，1927年8月5日于柏林发布。第36号

战争器材法。
1927年7月27日。

国会已决议通过以下法律，并经帝国参议院同意特此颁布：

§ 1
禁止进出口各类战争器材（武器、弹药及其他器材），以及为出口目的制造此类器材。

§ 2
供国内使用的战争器材，不得制造、储存或进行交易。

§ 3
除非第7条另有规定，否则以下产品受第1和第2条规定的约束：
1. 各类火炮和掷雷器，及其炮管车架和炮架；特殊附件。
2. 用于第1项所列武器的炮弹和弹药。

c) 不再属于任何国家国防军的武装，但仍可用于军事用途并指定用于战争目的。

7. 指定用于战争目的的、用于发射或投掷炸弹、鱼雷、水雷及其他类型炮弹的装置和机器。

für Schienen sowie dessen Sonderzubehör und die besonderen

in allem auszubilden,was die Artillerie,die Verwendung von

griffsmethoden sowie die für Kriegszwecke bestimmten Entver-
nungsmesser,Scheinwerfer,Anlagen für drahtlose Telegra-
phie und Unterwasser-Signalgeben betrifft.

a) der in den Ziffern 1 bis 10,12,13,17,bis 20,22a aufge-
führten Erzeugnisse und der in Ziffer 29 aufgeführten

b) der in den Ziffern 11,14,bis 16,21,23b,25a,32,33 aufge-

43. Folgende Sprengstoffe,die einen Bestandteil von Kriegsmitteln
jeder Art bilden können:

tersäureestergruppen an einem Kern ausser Pikrinsäure
und Trinitrotoluol.
b) Gepresste oder geschmolzene Pikrinsäure.

43. 下列可作为任何种类军械组成部分的炸药：
a) 除苦味酸和三硝基甲苯外，在一个核上带有三个或更多硝基或硝酸酯基团的硝基化合物。

当地军火商和运输商认为，附上的3月21日《字林西报》摘录中提到的军火批次，是指今年二月由挪威轮船“乌尔里克”号（Ulrikke）运抵上海的货物。
当地海关当局表示，如此大规模的运往上海的军火 shipment，若不正式告知承运货物的轮船名称等，是不可能交付的，而截至目前，通过任何常规渠道均未收到此类通知，因此他们得出结论，所指的军火必定是已通过“乌尔里克”号轮船交付的那批，这是最后一艘将军火运抵上海的轮船。

The Norwegian steamer "Ulrikka" arrived at Woosung on February 7 and discharged arms and ammunition which were consigned as follows : | No. of Consignment | Amount of Munitions | Parties to whom consigned | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | 1. | 19 cases of arms
143 cases of ammunition. | The Industry Trading Co. 20 Museum Road, | | 2. | 80 cases of rifles, sidearms,
and straps
1370 cases of ammunition. | The Societe Reghini, Canton Road. | The ship's manifest indicates that the Banque Franco-Chinois, No. 1 Quai de France, and Messrs. D'angelo Co., 20 Nanking Road, are also interested in the second consignment. Both the consignments were covered by huchows and were taken to the Arsenal in lighters belonging to D.G.M. Aronovsky, 6 Ezra Road, and the Hwa Fong Transportation Co., 35 Szechuen Road. Before arriving at Woosung the "Ulrikka" called at Amoy on January 21 owing to boiler trouble where the Customs Authorities seized 50 cases of percussion caps destined for Tientsin. She also transferred a quantity of arms and ammunition to a Chinese gunboat outside Canton. These munitions and the lots discharged at Shanghai were loaded at Gdingen in Poland but are of German manufacture. The s.s. Ulrikka left Shanghai on February 15 for Tientsin. Although no confirmation is available it is stated that the firm which supplies arms to the Chinese Navy at Canton is Messrs. Sander, Wieler & Co. which has offices at Hongkong, Canton and Shanghai. （批：A/D.C.I. Information. Copy for Shafire attached. 17/2 29） （签名：J. Kwieng A.C. Pol）

THE CHINA PRESS, WEDNESDAY, DECEMBER 12, 1928.

Arms Shipments
Consigned To China
Cannot Be Insured
(Reuter's Service)
London, Dec. 10.—Replying to a
question in the House of Commons
today Mr. G. Locker-Lampson,
Under-Secretary of State for For-
eign Affairs, said that the Institute
of London Underwriters had reach-
ed an agreement with the under-
writing associations of France, the
Netherlands, Greece, Japan, Poland,
Switzerland, Yugo-Slavia and the
United States prohibiting the insur-
ance of arms and munitions destin-
ed for China. He added that favor-
able replies had been received from
the underwriting associations of
Austria, Bulgaria, Denmark, Sweden
and Turkey, but that the agreement
had not yet been formally adopted.
Germany passed a law in March
prohibiting the insurance of arms
destined for China.

SHANGHAI. The Norwegian S.S. "BAUNE", 683 tons, recently
employed arms-running, arrived at Shanghai from Hongkong
on 28th December last via Walfis Bay (Aug/28) and Straits
consigned to O. Thoresen & Co.

The Norwegian Steamer "Baune" did not arrive
at Shanghai on the date mentioned above via Walfis Bay.

SHANGHAI MERCURY, THURSDAY, NOVEMBER 29, 1928.
57 P.O. 8760/31

THE MYSTERIOUS BAUNE.
Master Says Arms Cargo Landed in the North.
Big Consignment From Europe.
Adventures at Walfis Bay and Batavia.

A great deal of interest has been aroused in Hongkong by the flying visit of the Norwegian s.s. Baune, a little craft of 683 tons, which has managed to draw the limelight upon herself and her crew by her recent movements.

The Baune was generally supposed to be running large quantities of war munitions to China, and when the vessel passed rather hurriedly through the Colony's waters on Wednesday it was suspected that she had a big consignment for Canton.

The Master's Story.
The former master of the ship, Mr. Monsen, in an interview with the Hongkong Daily Press representative gave his own version of his ship's adventures and what is printed below is entirely his account.

European Powers have imposed a self-denying ordinance in the matter of shipping arms to China, so this little vessel, whose present owners are the Velhal Company of Hogisond, is strictly engaged on private enterprise.

Mr. Monsen was reticent with regard to the ship's movements but expressed himself with some eloquence on recent visits to Walfis Bay and Batavia of which accounts were cabled some time ago by Reuter.

Arms on Board.
Mr. Monsen, whose present whereabouts we are not at liberty to divulge, told our representative that it was quite true that he had recently landed a cargo of arms and ammunition in China.

"I was acting," he said, "under the instructions of an Englishman who claimed American nationality. The shippers were Germans and the rifles were from Poland and Denmark, Germany, Finland and Austria, and the cartridges from Denmark and Austria."

Landed at Newchwang.
"And where did you land them?"
"At Newchwang, North of Peking and Dairen, in the Gulf of Chili."
"There was," he declared, "no mystery about it. The munitions were landed in public and the Customs made no query."
"And who were the arms consigned to, Mr. Monsen?"
"That I shall not divulge at present. But later I shall be able to give full particulars of the deal. By no means the last has been heard of this affair."
"At Newchwang," he continued, "I took in a cargo of beans, and after calling at Dairen to take more cargo I came South to Hongkong where I took on board a pilot and went straight up to Canton. That was on November 14. Then I came down here and it was on Tuesday that the Hongkong police searched the ship, from stem to stern but found absolutely no trace of contraband.
"It was," Mr. Monsen added, "at Hongkong and not at Canton, as I see has been stated, that I signed on a new crew.
"The publicity and all the trouble that I have experienced has very much got on my nerves. I felt very near a nervous breakdown and I have put the Chief Officer, Mr. Hausen, in charge."

Batavia and Walfis Bay.
After expressing sympathy with regard to Mr. Monsen's impaired health our representative questioned him as to what has been described as the "remarkable behaviour" of the Baune at Walfis Bay in British West Africa and again at Batavia, Java. Mr. Monsen said with some heat that the "remarkable behaviour" had been entirely on the part of the harbour officials at those two places.
"It is quite untrue that at Batavia I refused to allow the Harbour Master and the police on board. As a matter of fact the Harbour Master actually took me with him in his motor boat when he came no board. I offered them the run of the ship but they didn't seem at all anxious to get their uniforms dirty by grubbing about in the bunkers. But there was no need. There were no munitions in the bunkers for the simple reason that the bunkers would not hold a quarter the amount we had on board."
The ship left Batavia hurriedly, he then explained, entirely because he had only just enough coal to take him to his destination, and not to allow him to wait about at Batavia!
With regard to the trouble at Walfis Bay, Mr. Monsen declared that he was never within the three miles territorial water limit. He did not produce his papers there because he was under no obligation to do so, being outside the limit of jurisdiction.
"The Baune has been searched twice before but I will not say where," said Mr. Monsen repeating in conclusion, that by no means the last had been heard of his former command.
The ship left here on Tuesday afternoon, after a thorough search by the police. Nothing suspicious was found, and her papers were in order.
Mr. Monsen is a young, well set up man, an obvious sailor and game for adventures.

(批：Local 30/11)

神秘的“BAUNE”号。
船长称军火货物在北方登陆。
来自欧洲的大批货物。
在沃尔维斯湾和巴达维亚的冒险经历。

挪威籍蒸汽船“Baune”号，一艘683吨的小型船只，因其近期的动向而使自己及其船员成为公众关注的焦点，在香港引起了极大兴趣。

人们普遍认为“Baune”号正向中国运送大量战争军需品，当该船于周三相当匆忙地穿过殖民地水域时，有人怀疑它有一大批货物要运往广州。

船长的说法。
该船前船长蒙森先生（Mr. Monsen）在接受《香港每日新闻》代表采访时，讲述了他自己版本的船舶冒险经历，下文刊登的内容完全基于他的陈述。

欧洲列强在向中国运输军火问题上实施了自我约束法令，因此这艘目前由 Hogisond 的 Velhal 公司所有的小型船只，严格来说是从事私人企业活动。

蒙森先生对船舶的动向守口如瓶，但在谈及最近访问沃尔维斯湾和巴达维亚时却滔滔不绝，路透社此前曾电报报道过相关消息。

船上有军火。
蒙森先生，我们不便透露其目前下落，他告诉我们的代表，他最近确实在中国卸下了一批军火和弹药。

“我是按照一名声称拥有美国国籍的英国人的指示行事，”他说。“发货人是德国人，步枪来自波兰、丹麦、德国、芬兰和奥地利，子弹来自丹麦和奥地利。”

在新营口登陆。
“你在哪里卸货？”
“在北京以北和大连以北的新营口，位于直隶湾。”
他宣称：“这没有什么神秘之处。军火是公开卸下的，海关没有提出任何质疑。”
“那么这些军火是发给谁的，蒙森先生？”
“我目前不会透露。但稍后我将能够提供交易的详细情况。此事远未结束。”
“在新营口，”他继续说道，“我装上了一批豆类货物，在停靠大连加装更多货物后，我南下前往香港，在那里我聘请了一名引水员，然后直接前往广州。那是11月14日。然后我来到这里，周二香港警察对船只进行了从头到尾的搜查，但完全没有发现违禁品的踪迹。
“正如我所见有人声称的那样，”蒙森先生补充道，“我是在香港而不是在广州招募了新船员。
“ publicity 和我所经历的所有麻烦让我非常紧张。我感觉快要精神崩溃了，所以我让大副豪森先生（Mr. Hausen）负责指挥。”

巴达维亚和沃尔维斯湾。
在对蒙森先生受损的健康表示同情后，我们的代表询问了他关于“Baune”号在西非英属沃尔维斯湾以及在爪哇巴达维亚被描述为“异常行为”的情况。蒙森先生有些激动地说，“异常行为”完全出自这两个地方的港口官员。
“说我在巴达维亚拒绝允许港务长和警察上船是完全不实的。事实上，港务长上船时确实带我乘坐了他的摩托艇。我让他们随意检查船只，但他们似乎一点也不急于通过在煤舱中翻找弄脏他们的制服。但这没有必要。煤舱里没有军需品，原因很简单，煤舱连我们船上所载数量的四分之一都装不下。”
他随后解释说，船只匆忙离开巴达维亚，完全是因为他只有刚好够到达目的地的煤炭，而不允许他在巴达维亚逗留！
关于在沃尔维斯湾的麻烦，蒙森先生宣称他从未进入三海里领水界限内。他在那里没有出示文件，因为他没有义务这样做，因为他处于管辖范围之外。
“‘Baune’号以前曾被搜查过两次，但我不会说在哪里，”蒙森先生在结束时重复道，关于他以前指挥的这艘船，事情远未结束。
该船在周二下午离开这里，此前经过警方的彻底搜查。未发现可疑物品，其文件齐全。
蒙森先生是一位年轻、身材健硕的男子，显然是一名水手，且热衷于冒险。

（批注：本地 11月30日）

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, APRIL 19, 1929.

Lawsuit Over Arms Deal Is
Concluded At Tientsin

Italian Ordered To Pay General Chang Chin-Yao,
Former Governor Of Hunan, $44,000 And Inter-
est; Deal Involved Nearly $1,000,000

Tientsin, Apr. 10.
Judge Rapex of the Italian Court for China rendered judgment in the case of Chang Chin-yao v. E. Marzoli on Monday morning and declared that the defendant, Mr. Marzoli, was bound to pay back to the plaintiff the sum of $44,576.52 with interest and costs.
The case had been before last month's sitting of the Italian Court for China at Tientsin.
The above decision closes a long standing question in the Italian Court. In case of appeal by either party, the matter should be interposed with a higher Court in Italy.
The case originated from a contract made in April 1919 (before the Arms Embargo) between Mr. Marzoli and Gen. Chang Chin-yao, then Governor of Hunan, by which the former engaged himself to supply the latter with a certain quantity of war materials for a total amount of $988,800. In accordance with the contract the buyer paid one-third of the said amount, net $313,000, and engaged himself to provide the seller with the import huohao within 20 days from the signature of the contract. The contract did not go through.

Prisoner Of Gen. Feng
General Chang Chin-yao tried several times to settle the question in connection with the unfulfilled contract without result and he therefore made his first application in January, 1925 to the Italian Court. His petition was then rejected on the ground that the signature on the power of attorney he gave to his representative was not legalized. Being at that time a prisoner of General Feng Yu-hsiang he was not able to go further with the matter.
The question came up again before the Court in March 1928 and the plaintiff was then successful in establishing his personal interest in the case against the contention of the defendant that it was for the Provincial Government of Hunan to bring the case before the Court, and not its ex-Governor.

Arms Embargo Mentioned
In October last the case came up for the third time before the Court, Gen. Chang Chin-yao claiming the right to receive back the money he had paid the defendant. He based his request on the ground that he was not able to supply the import huohao on account of the Arms Embargo by the Powers, which was declared soon after the signature of the contract, and that he did not pay the other two-thirds of the amount due owing to having found that Mr. Marzoli had cashed the first instalment notwithstanding the written engagement that this should be kept in the Bank until the final completion of the contract.
The Court then ruled (1) that plaintiff could not claim a case of force majeure in not providing the huohao as the Powers Embargo did not prevent the Chinese Government from issuing any huohao it liked; (2) that plaintiff not having protested when he heard of the serious fault on the part of the defendant in cashing the money, and in not having made his refusal to pay any further instalment clearly consequent on the want of observance, on the part of defendant, of the stipulated clause, had now lost the legal right to stand on this ground to justify legally his action in 1919.
Therefore, the judgment rendered in October, 1928, declared the legal fault for the breach of contract rested on the plaintiff without deceit on his part, and that defendant had the right to claim compensation for the expected net profits on the contract and to the reimbursement of any sum paid by him as a direct consequence of the non-execution of the contract on the part of the plaintiff. The liquidation of the accounts was postponed until the next session of the Court.

Claims Payment Of $300,000
The case came for the fourth time before the Italian Court on the 16th ult., when the plaintiff submitted his pleadings concluding with the request to have the defendant bound to pay him back at least the sum of $124,752.04 with the legal compound interest of 5 per cent. per annum from June 10, 1920, pointing out that, in accordance with his figures, defendant expected in 1919 a net profit of 17.1 per cent. while with the actual request the profits increase to 19.1 per cent. Thus plaintiff's actual loss of money was 60.2 per cent. without having received anything.
Defendant concluded his pleading by requesting the plaintiff be bound to pay him a further sum of $173,692.30 with interest from June 1920.

《字林西报》，1929年4月19日，星期五。

天津军火交易诉讼案结案

意大利人被判向前湖南省长张敬尧将军支付44,000美元及利息；交易涉及金额近100万美元

天津，4月10日电。
意大利在华法院法官拉佩克斯（Rapex）于周一上午对张敬尧诉E.马尔佐利（E. Marzoli）一案作出判决，宣布被告马尔佐利先生须向原告偿还44,576.52美元，并支付利息及诉讼费。

该案曾于上月在天津的意大利在华法院开庭审理。

上述裁决结束了意大利法院中一桩长期悬而未决的案件。若任何一方提出上诉，此事将提交意大利更高一级法院处理。

本案源于1919年4月（武器禁运前）马尔佐利先生与时任湖南省长的张敬尧将军之间签订的一份合同，前者承诺向后者供应一定数量的军用物资，总金额为988,800美元。根据合同，买方支付了该金额的三分之一，即净额313,000美元，并承诺在合同签订后20天内向卖方提供进口货照（huohao）。该合同最终未能履行。

冯玉祥将军的囚徒

张敬尧将军曾多次尝试解决与未履行合约相关的问题，但均无结果，因此他于1925年1月首次向意大利法院提出申请。当时他的申请被驳回，理由是他授予代表的授权委托书上的签名未经公证合法化。由于当时他是冯玉祥将军的囚徒，无法进一步处理此事。

1928年3月，该问题再次提交法院审理，原告成功确立了其在本案中的个人利害关系，驳回了被告关于此案应由湖南省政府而非前任省长向法院提起的主张。

提及武器禁运

去年10月，该案第三次提交法院审理，张敬尧将军声称有权收回已支付给被告的款项。他提出请求的理由是，由于列强在合同签订后不久即宣布实施武器禁运，导致他无法提供进口货照（huohao）；此外，尽管有书面约定首付款应存入银行直至合同最终履行完毕，但他发现马尔佐利先生已将首付款兑现，因此未支付其余三分之二的应付款项。

法院随后裁定：(1) 原告不能以不可抗力为由主张未能提供货照（huohao），因为列强的禁运令并未阻止中国政府签发其希望签发的任何货照（huohao）；(2) 原告在得知被告兑现款项这一严重过错时未提出抗议，且未将其拒绝支付后续分期付款的行为明确归因于被告未遵守规定条款，因此现已丧失以此为由在法律上正当化其1919年行为的权利。

因此，1928年10月作出的判决宣布，违约的法律责任在于原告，且原告并无欺诈行为；被告有权就合同预期的净利润要求赔偿，并有权要求偿还因其未履行合同而直接导致的任何已付款项。账目清算推迟至法院下一次开庭进行。

索赔30万美元

上月16日，该案第四次提交意大利法院审理，原告提交诉状，最后要求被告至少偿还124,752.04美元，并支付自1920年6月10日起按年利率5%计算的法定复利，同时指出，根据其计算，被告在1919年的预期净利润为17.1%，而根据实际诉求，利润增至19.1%。因此，原告在未收到任何货物的情况下，实际资金损失为60.2%。

被告在结束其诉辩时，要求判令原告向其支付额外款项173,692.30美元，并支付自1920年6月起算的利息。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
No. 10. 8760/55
Date 9. 11. 28

PEKING AND TIENTSIN TIMES TUESDAY, OCTOBER 30, 1928.

ARBITRAGE AT
TIENTSIN.
HEARING IN THE ITALIAN
COURT.
JUDGMENT FOR MR.
MARZOLI.

Yesterday afternoon in the Italian Court for China, sitting at Tientsin, His Honour Judge Raffaele Rapex gave judgment in the case in which General Chang Chin-yao, a former Governor of Hunan, sued Mr. Egidio Marzoli, an Italian merchant of Tientsin, for the return of a sum of $313,000 alleged to have been paid him as a first instalment on a contract for the supply of arms.

This suit was first mentioned before a Court in 1923 but proceedings could not then be continued as the Court did not consider the power of attorney given to the then representative of General Chang Chin-yao was in order and ordered that he must obtain properly recognised authority. On February 24th of the present year, the case was again mentioned before His Honour Judge Rapex sitting at Tientsin when Mr. A. Martinella appeared as the representative of General Chung Chin-yao. The Court found that his powers of attorney were in order and subsequently the preliminary plea of the defence was dealt with.

At the present session of the Italian Court the case has been gone into at length. His Honour Judge Rapex was assisted by two assessors, Mr. P. Bonetti and Dr. Giavotto.

Plaintiff was represented by Mr. A. Martinella and the counsel for the defence was Dr. Hoselitz.

Plaintiff's original statement of his case alleged that in April 1919 he was Governor of Hunan and had then contracted with defendant to supply him with 10,000 rifles, 10,000,000 cartridges for the same, mitrailleuses, and 200,000 mitrailleuse cartridges, at a total price of $938,800. One-third of the contract money, viz, $313,000, was paid into a Bank in Tientsin in the name of M. Marzoli but for various reasons the goods were never consigned General Chang, it was alleged.

Defendant stated the alleged non-delivery was due to a breach of contract on the part of General Chang Chin-yao and that he had suffered damage to the extent of the sum of $526,000 as a result of the said breach of contract which he alleged against the plaintiff. It was stated that General Chang is now residing in Mukden.

In finding for the defendant with costs, His Honour Judge Rapex read his Judgment which was long and detailed. A summary of the Judgment declares that the breach of contract rests with General Chang Chin-yao with regard to the contract stipulated on April 6th, 1919, between himself and Mr. Egidio Marzoli, and that as a consequence the said General Chang Chin-yao is responsible to the other party for damages. It leaves to further judgment the determination of the amount of the indemnity to be paid by the said General Chang Chin-yao to Mr. Marzoli in accordance with this decision.

This decision, it is understood in practice simply means dismissal of plaintiff's claim as plaintiff is a Chinese citizen and therefore not subject to the jurisdiction of the Honourable Court for the purpose of the enforcement of the damages.

《京津泰晤士报》，1928年10月30日，星期二。

天津仲裁。
意大利法院听证。
马尔佐利先生胜诉。

昨日下午，在天津开庭的意大利在华法院，拉斐尔·拉佩克斯（Raffaele Rapex）法官对前湖南省长张敬尧将军起诉天津意大利商人埃吉迪奥·马尔佐利（Egidio Marzoli）先生一案作出判决，要求后者归还据称作为军火供应合同首付款支付的313,000美元。

该案曾于1923年首次在法院提及，但当时诉讼无法继续，因为法院认为授予张敬尧将军当时代表的授权委托书不符合规定，命令其必须获得正式认可的授权。今年2月24日，该案再次在天津由拉佩克斯法官审理，A.马丁内拉（A. Martinella）先生作为张敬尧将军的代表出庭。法院认定其授权委托书符合规定，随后处理了被告方的初步抗辩。

在意大利法院本次庭审中，对该案进行了详尽审理。拉佩克斯法官由两名陪审员P.博内蒂（P. Bonetti）先生和贾沃托（Giavotto）博士协助。

原告由A.马丁内拉先生代理，被告辩护律师为霍塞利茨（Hoselitz）博士。

原告最初的案情陈述称，1919年4月他担任湖南省长，并与被告签订合同，由被告向其供应10,000支步枪、1,000万发配套子弹、机枪以及20万发机枪子弹，总价为938,800美元。合同款项的三分之一，即313,000美元，以M.马尔佐利的名义存入天津一家银行，但据称由于各种原因，货物从未发给张将军。

被告称，所谓未交付是由于张敬尧将军违约所致，并称因原告的上述违约行为，他遭受了高达526,000美元的损失。据悉，张将军现居沈阳。

拉佩克斯法官在判决被告胜诉并由原告承担诉讼费时，宣读了冗长而详细的判决书。判决摘要声明，关于1919年4月6日张敬尧将军与埃吉迪奥·马尔佐利先生之间规定的合同，违约责任在于张敬尧将军，因此该将军须向另一方承担损害赔偿责任。至于张敬尧将军根据此决定应向马尔佐利先生支付的赔偿金额，留待进一步判决确定。

据了解，这一裁决在实际操作中仅意味着驳回原告的索赔，因为原告是中国公民，因此不受本庭管辖以执行损害赔偿。

PEKING & TIENTSIN TIMES. THURSDAY, NOVEMBER 1, 1928.

ARMS CASE AT TIEN-TSIN.
STATEMENT BY MR. A. MARTINELLA.

Mr. A. Martinella, representative of the plaintiff in the case of General Chang Chin-yao v. Marzoli in the Italian Court for China, has sent us the following statement with regard to the decision in this case:
“In the case Chang Chin-yao—Marzoli the Italian Court rendered their judgment recognizing that plaintiff is to be held responsible for damages for breach of contract having rendered impossible the consignment of the arms contracted for on account of having not produced the import luchao and not completed the payments in accordance with the contract.”
“The fixing of the damages has been left to a further discussion in order to ascertain what amount, if any, defendant has to return to plaintiff from what he has received as first payment.”
“It is understood that in accordance with the judgment rendered as above, the plaintiff is petitioning the Italian Court to get a final statement about the damages.”

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, THURSDAY, OCTOBER 25, 1928

REPORTED SEIZURE
OF MUNITIONS

Small Vessel with Two Tons of
Arms Captured at
Woosung

The "Eastern Times" yesterday
published the story of the seizure
of a large quantity of munitions
from a vessel which was about to
enter Woosung on Tuesday.
From the report, it would appear
that information had been received
by the Woosung Fort authorities
that a small vessel would shortly
enter port in a secret manner and
that it had on board a large con-
signment of munitions.
Gen. Teng Tsen-chuan, the Fort
Commander, issued instructions to
his subordinate to be on the look-
out for such a vessel and, at 11
a.m. on Tuesday, their efforts were
rewarded when a small vessel was
sighted and ordered to stop.
A thorough search was made and
on board was found 109 chests of
7.9 ammunition, four trench mortars,
32 chests of field gun shells, one
case of gunpowder, 64 cases of
"white medicine," etc. In all, it
is said, the consignment weighed
two tons.
An inquiry had been ordered, the
vessel meanwhile being detained.

THE CHINA PRESS, FRIDAY, SEPTEMBER ...

Drastic Laws Against Criminal Use Of Arms
Framed By Nationalists

Manufacture, Possession Or Traffic With Criminal Intent May Bring Five Year Prison Sentence

(Kuo Min News Agency)
Nanking, Sept. 13.—A set of regulations governing the manufacture, possession, transportation and traffic in fire-arms has been drawn up by the Military Council and will soon be promulgated by the Nationalist Government. A translation of the regulations is given below:

Article I. The manufacturing, possessing, transporting, and trafficking in fire-arms and ammunition with any criminal intent shall be punishable by imprisonment from six months to five years. The "manufacturing, possessing, transporting and trafficking in fire-arms and ammunition for other people known to have criminal intentions shall likewise be subject to the same term of imprisonment.

Article II. The manufacturing, possessing, transporting and trafficking in fire-arms and ammunition without first obtaining proper authorization and permission shall, upon failure to produce satisfactory reasons for not having the proper authorization and permission, be punishable by imprisonment and hard work for a period not exceeding three years, or by a fine not exceeding five hundred dollars.

Article III. The Police or any other authorities concerned, failing in the prompt enforcement of the preceding articles or conniving at or becoming accomplices in the violation thereof, shall be punished according to the provisions of the preceding articles.

Article IV. Other measures of punishment as provided in the Criminal Code which do not conflict with these rules may be adopted.

Article V. These regulations shall become effective upon promulgation.

《大美晚报》，9月某日，星期五……

国民党制定严厉法律打击犯罪使用武器

制造、持有或出于犯罪意图交易者可判处五年监禁

（国民新闻社）
南京，9月13日电。——军事委员会已起草一套关于枪支制造、持有、运输和交易的规章，并将由国民政府不久后颁布。规章译文如下：

第一条 凡出于任何犯罪意图制造、持有、运输和交易枪支及弹药者，应处以六个月以上五年以下监禁。明知他人有犯罪意图而为其制造、持有、运输和交易枪支及弹药者，同样适用上述刑期。

第二条 未事先获得适当授权和许可而制造、持有、运输和交易枪支及弹药者，若不能提出没有适当授权和许可的令人满意的理由，应处以不超过三年的监禁及苦役，或处以不超过五百元的罚款。

第三条 警察或其他有关当局若未能迅速执行上述条款，或对违反行为纵容包庇、成为共犯，应按上述条款规定予以处罚。

第四条 可采用刑法典中规定的与本规则不冲突的其他惩罚措施。

第五条 本规章自颁布之日起生效。

PISTOL SMUGGLING.
AN ARREST AND A CONFESSION.

The Sannomiya police took a young
man into custody at Moto-machi on the
night of the 13th instant. The youth, a

Osaka gun dealers and concealed mil-

Godown on No. 2 pier. The Kobe police

police for the rounding up of the whole
gang.

Light artillery, machine guns,
rifles, small arms and other
munitions of war, said to have cost
in excess of G.$250,000 and to be
one of the largest consignments of
military material ever brought to
Shanghai for the Nationalist Gov-
ernment, are being unloaded to-day
at the China Merchants Lower
Wharf from the Norwegian str.
Childar, which arrived here several
days ago from Hamburg, Germany.
Operating under charter to the
R. C. Rickmers Line, the main part
of the Childar's cargo consist of
munitions, it is stated. The exact
quantity aboard, together with the
precise value of same, could not be
learned from the Shanghai re-
presentative of the Rickmers Line
who stated that he was not at
liberty to give out this information.
It is expected that the munitions
will be transported from Shanghai
either to the capital or inland to
some military centre. The Childar,
which entered at Shanghai on Oct.

ing has been completed.

CONFIDENTIEL
MEMORANDUM.
（印：MUNICIPAL POLICE / I.D. REGISTRY / 8760/116.）

The Cargo shipped from Sabang on 27 September by the German
s.s. "LUNEBURG" was discharged at Marseilles and not at Ham-
burg as expected.
Shippers of these arms are "The Industrial Export China Co."
at Brussels, whose agents at Hongkong are Laurent and Krebs.
A further shipment was made by the s.s. "HAVELAND" of the
Hamburg America Line, consigned to General Cohen. The arms were
taken on board at Antwerp and discharged at Colombo for the
purpose of having them reshipped by the s.s. "SAUERLAND" of
the same company, which arrived at Hongkong on the 12th of Oc-
tober. This vessel also carried a consignment of arms which she
discharged at Colombo, and she did not take with her the arms
unloaded by the "HAVELAND", most probably on instructions of
the Head Office at Hamburg.
On arrival at Hongkong on the 2nd of October the "Haveland" was
seized by order of the Supreme Court at the request of General
Cohen, who claimed repayment of the sums advanced on the cargo
left behind at Colombo. It appears that after the execution of
a bond in the amount of Gold $ 25,000.- (?) by the agents of the
Hamburg America Line the vessel was released on the 8th of Oc-
tober, pending the decision of the Supreme Court. It appears
further that parties have come to an amicable settlement of their
dispute, whereby it was agreed that the cargo left behind at
Colombo would be delivered by another steamer.
The Hamburg America Line seems to have decided to stop all further
shipments of arms to China by her steamers. The North German Lloyd
seems to have taken that attitude from the very beginning. The
"Rickmers" steamers appear to be frequently involved in obscure
transactions.
Regular supplies of arms seem to be made to Canton however by
Japanese and Norwegian steamers.
（批：Jawm / ?）
（批：Vol）
Shanghai, 22 October 1931.

机密
备忘录。
（印章：警务处 / 身份登记室 / 8760/116.）

9月27日由德国轮船“吕讷堡”号（s.s. "LUNEBURG"）从沙璜（Sabang）装运的货物在马赛卸下，而非如预期的在汉堡卸下。
这批武器的发货人是布鲁塞尔的“中国工业出口公司”（The Industrial Export China Co.），其在香港的代理人为劳伦特和克雷布斯（Laurent and Krebs）。
另一批货物由汉堡美洲航运公司（Hamburg America Line）的“哈维兰”号（s.s. "HAVELAND"）装运，收货人为科恩将军（General Cohen）。武器在安特卫普装上船，并在科伦坡卸下，目的是由同一公司的“绍尔兰”号（s.s. "SAUERLAND"）重新装运，该轮于10月12日抵达香港。这艘船还携带了一批在科伦坡卸下的武器，但它并未带走由“哈维兰”号卸下的武器，这很可能是遵照汉堡总行的指示。
“哈维兰”号于10月2日抵达香港后，应科恩将军的请求，被最高法院下令扣押，科恩将军要求偿还为留在科伦坡的货物垫付的款项。看来，在汉堡美洲航运公司的代理人出具了一份金额为金币25,000元（？）的保函后，该船于10月8日获释，等待最高法院的裁决。此外，各方似乎已就争议达成和解，同意由另一艘轮船交付留在科伦坡的货物。
汉堡美洲航运公司似乎已决定停止由其轮船向中国进一步装运武器。北德意志劳埃德公司（North German Lloyd）似乎从一开始就采取了这种态度。“里克默斯”（Rickmers）轮船似乎经常卷入不透明的交易。
然而，日本和挪威轮船似乎定期向广州供应武器。
（批注：Jawm / ?）
（批注：Vol）
上海，1931年10月22日。

Subject (in full) Munitions on board the s.s.'Vogtland' and 'Duisburg'.

Made by and Forwarded by D. I. Ross

With reference to the attached reports on the subject of consignments of munitions on board the s.s.'Vogtland' and 'Duisburg', inquiries show that following the threats of both Nanking and Canton to boycott those countries whose shipping companies do not comply with their wishes especially in regard to the shipment of arms, the Hamburg Amerika Line cabled their office in Hamburg to cancel all orders for shipments of arms destined for China.

In consequence the vessels of this company engaged in this trade were instructed to discharge arms ordered by the Canton Government at certain ports. As a result the s.s.'Vogtland' discharged a cargo of 667 cases of rifle ammunition at Sabang, Netherlands India on August 25, 1931. Here it remained until September 27 when it was loaded on to the s.s.'Luneburg' (H.A.Line) for transportation to Germany, on the instructions of the Hamburg Amerika Line office in Hamburg. This particular consignment was ordered through Shenkers and Co.,Hamburg, by the Ministry of War, Government of Canton. In addition to this shipment the 'Vogtland' also carried 910 cases of rifle ammunition which had been ordered from Walter Hell(?) Hamburg, by the Nanking Government, through Carlowitz and Co., 220 Szechuen Road, Shanghai. This shipment was discharged into lighters off Woosung on or about September 9, 1931, under Customs supervision and landed at the Woosung Railway Wharf for transportation to Nanking.

As regards the s.s.'Duisburg' which was carrying a consignment of 239 cases of rifle ammunition destined for Canton,
this vessel attempted to discharge same also at Sabang but was prevented from doing so by the Netherlands Indian Government. Therefore

制作及报送人 D. I. Ross

关于附件中有关“福格特兰”号和“杜伊斯堡”号船上军火货物的报告，调查显示，鉴于南京和广州双方威胁要抵制那些航运公司不顺应其意愿（特别是关于武器装运方面）的国家，汉堡美洲航运公司已向其汉堡办事处发电报，取消所有运往中国的武器装运订单。

因此，该公司从事此项贸易的船只奉命在某些港口卸下广东政府订购的武器。结果是，“福格特兰”号于1931年8月25日在荷属东印度的沙璜卸下了667箱步枪弹药。该批货物在此停留至9月27日，随后根据汉堡美洲航运公司汉堡办事处的指示，装上汉堡美洲航运公司的“吕讷堡”号（s.s.'Luneburg'）运往德国。这批特定货物是由广东政府国防部通过汉堡的申克尔斯公司（Shenkers and Co., Hamburg）订购的。除这批货物外，“福格特兰”号还载有910箱步枪弹药，这是南京政府通过上海四川路220号的礼和洋行（Carlowitz and Co.）向汉堡的沃尔特·赫尔（Walter Hell(?)）订购的。这批货物大约在1931年9月9日在吴淞口外驳船上卸下，受海关监管，并登陆吴淞铁路码头以便运往南京。

With regard to the attempted transshipment of arms
from the s.s. "Vogtland" and "Duisburg" of the Hamburg
Amerika Line at Sabang, efforts were made by the Mi-
nistry of Foreign Affairs at Canton to have the consign-
ment of arms "bought by the Canton Authorities from Eu-
rope for the purpose of suppressing bandits and communists"
and discharged at Sabang (N.E.I.) from the s.s. "Vogtland"
transshipped to Canton. A letter of introduction from
the Netherlands Consul at Canton was applied for by the
authorities there on behalf of Mr.C.W.Leung, who would be
sent to Netherlands' India to claim this cargo. This appli-
cation however was refused whereas at the same time the Head
Office of the Holland East Asia Line at Rotterdam issued
instructions to its agent at Canton not to have the
cargo transported to Canton by any one of its steamers.
No information is available as to what decision has been
arrived at with regard to the cargo discharged from the s.s.
"Vogtland" at Sabang.
As regards the s.s. "Duisburg" it appears that after
the refusal of the Netherlands Indian Government to have
transhipment made at Sabang, the receivers intended to have
same effected at Manilla. Before this port was reached
however, the arms were claimed by the Nanking Government.
The agents of the Hamburg Amerika Line at Hongkong informed the
representative of the Canton Government, General M.A.Cohen
thereof, and General Cohen thereupon obtained a ruling from
the Supreme Court at Hongkong, whereby the s.s. "Duisburg" was
detained, pending a decision concerning the delivery of the
arms. General Cohen, who had all the documents in hand, re-
ceived the cargo and the vessel was allowed to proceed.
Since both Nanking and Canton are threatening a boycott
of those countries whose shipping companies do not comply
with

关于汉堡美洲航运公司“福格特兰”号和“杜伊斯堡”号在沙璜试图转运武器一事，广州外交部曾努力促使将“福格特兰”号在沙璜（荷属东印度）卸下的、“由广东当局从欧洲购买用于剿匪和反共”的武器货物转运至广州。广州当局代表梁C.W.先生（Mr.C.W.Leung）申请了一封由荷兰驻广州领事出具的介绍信，梁先生将被派往荷属东印度认领这批货物。然而，该申请被拒绝，与此同时，鹿特丹的荷兰东亚航运公司（Holland East Asia Line）总行向其广州代理人发出指示，不得由其任何轮船将该货物运往广州。
目前尚无关于“福格特兰”号在沙璜卸下的货物最终如何处理的信息。
至于“杜伊斯堡”号，看来在荷属东印度政府拒绝在沙璜进行转运后，收货人打算在马尼拉进行转运。然而，在抵达该港口之前，南京政府声称拥有这批武器。汉堡美洲航运公司在香港的代理人将此情况通知了广东政府代表M.A.科恩将军，科恩将军随后从香港最高法院获得裁决，扣留“杜伊斯堡”号，以待关于武器交付的决定。科恩将军手中握有所有文件，接收了货物，该船随后获准离开。
由于南京和广州都在威胁抵制那些航运公司不顺应其

with their wishes, a general hands-off attitude is taken
by most of them.

The aeroplanes, seized by Nanking, from the German
s.s. "Bona" (which seizure caused a boycott of German firms
in Canton) were made by Junkers in Sweden.

The cargo on board the s.s. "Vogtland" consisted of
5000 guns and 2,000,000 cartridges.

The cargo on board the s.s. "Duisburg" appears to have
been smaller.

The guns are of Checkoslovakian make, whereas the
ammunition and revolvers (Mausers) come most probably from
Belgium (Fabrique Nationale d'Armes de Guerre at Herstal?).
General Cohen, supposed to be a British subject of Hebrew
origin, born in Canada, is a well known adventurer, who
takes advantage of the disturbed conditions in China. For-
merly he was the body-guard of Dr. Sun Yat-sen, but he has
been promoted since to the rank of Brigadier General of the
Cantonese Army.

Shanghai, 1st October 1931.

On the 27th of September the cargo discharged by the s.s.
"Vogtland" in lighters at Sabang was loaded on the German
s.s. "Luneburg" of the Hamburg Amerika Line in order to be
returned to Hamburg.

Shanghai, 2nd October 1931.

意愿的国家，大多数国家对此采取了普遍的不干涉态度。

南京从德国轮船“博纳”号（s.s. "Bona"）扣押的飞机（此次扣押导致广州抵制德国商行）是由容克斯（Junkers）在瑞典制造的。

“福格特兰”号船上的货物包括5000支枪和2,000,000发子弹。

“杜伊斯堡”号船上的货物似乎较少。

枪支为捷克斯洛伐克制造，而弹药和左轮手枪（毛瑟式）很可能来自比利时（赫斯塔尔的国营兵工厂 Fabrique Nationale d'Armes de Guerre at Herstal?）。

科恩将军，据信是出生于加拿大的希伯来裔英国臣民，是一位著名的冒险家，利用中国的动荡局势谋利。他曾是孙中山博士的保镖，但此后已晋升为粤军旅长。

上海，1931年10月1日。

MEMORANDUM.

In the evening of the 25th of August 1931, the s.s.
"Vogtland" of the Hamburg America Line arrived at Sabang
after having called at Hamburg, Bremen, Rotterdam, Antwerp,
Colombo. She discharged at Sabang 667 cases of ammunition
and 239 cases of guns of a total weight of 90 tons, origi-
nating from Czechoslovakia and destined for Hongkong.
The consignees were unknown, but there is reason to suppose
that this cargo was destined for Canton. This cargo was
discharged in a lighter to await reshipment at an unknown
date, whereas no reason for this discharge was given, although
this might be due to lack of money of the ultimate receivers.
The steamer, having still on board a similar quantity of
cargo from Antwerp destined to the order of unknown consignees
at Shanghai, left Sabang in the morning of 26 August for
Penang, Singapore, Hongkong, Shanghai, Kobe and Yokohama.
Notice was received that the s.s. "Duisburg" of the Hamburg
America Line intended to discharge on the 5th of September
at Sabang 239 cases of arms and ammunition in the same manner,
whereupon orders were given by the Netherlands Indian Govern-
ment to prevent the discharge of this cargo.

备忘录。

1931年8月25日晚，汉堡-美洲航运公司（Hamburg America Line）的“福格特兰”号（s.s. "Vogtland"）轮船在停靠汉堡、不来梅、鹿特丹、安特卫普和科伦坡后抵达沙璜（Sabang）。该船在沙璜卸下了源自捷克斯洛伐克、运往香港的667箱弹药和239箱枪支，总重90吨。收货人不明，但有理由推测这批货物是运往广州的。这批货物被卸到驳船上，等待在未知日期重新装运，尽管未给出此次卸货的理由，但这可能是由于最终接收方资金短缺所致。该轮船上仍载有同样数量的从安特卫普启运、凭上海未知收货人指示交付的货物，于8月26日上午离开沙璜，前往槟城、新加坡、香港、上海、神户和横滨。随后收到通知称，汉堡-美洲航运公司的“杜伊斯堡”号（s.s. "Duisburg"）轮船计划于9月5日以同样方式在沙璜卸下239箱武器和弹药，荷兰东印度政府随即下令阻止该批货物的卸载。

REPORT

Subject (in full) Ammunition found on s.s. "Tjisadane".

Made by and Forwarded by D.I. Ross

With reference to the letter of September 29, from the
Netherlands Consulate-General, on the subject of the finding of
31438 rounds of ammunition on board the s.s. "Tjisadane", inquiries
show that the ammunition, which was wrapped up in local Chinese
newspapers of recent date and Sincere Co., wrapping paper, was
discovered by the ship's officers and turned over to the Customs
Authorities without any explanation whatsoever.

The Customs are of the opinion that the ammunition was
smuggled on board in Shanghai by certain local Chinese and destined
to be landed at Amoy for the use of bandits operating in the
Fukien province.

SHANGHAI, 29th September 1931.

Sir,

I have the honour to inform you that members
of the crew of the s. s. "Tjisadane" of the Java China
Japan Line discovered 31438 rounds of ammunition, which
were concealed on board of said steamer. Due report
was made to the Customs authorities, who might be able
to furnish further particulars. I may mention that
the ammunition in question was wrapped in local news-
papers of recent date, so that there is every reason to
suppose that the ammunition was brought on board after
the arrival of the vessel at Shanghai, with the inten-
tion to have it dispatched to ports in South China, whence
the steamer in question left.

I sent a copy of this letter to Mr. Sarly of the
French Police.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,

LOCAL CUSTOMS
31,420 Rounds Seized In

Tjisadane

The new J. C. J. L. s.s. Tjisadane,
on her maiden voyage to the Far
East, yielded no less than 31,420
rounds of Mauser pistol ammuni-
tion to Customs searchers, who
carried out their customary search
of incoming vessels on Wednesday
afternoon.

berthed at Holt's Wharf, Pootung.
The River Police co-operated with
the Customs searchers in their
search of the vessel and the dis-
covery was made at 1.30 p.m. after
several hours of thorough search-
ing.

No arrests are reported as
having been made.

THE SHANGHAI TIMES—FRIDAY, AUGUST 28, 1931.

SEIZURE OF VESSELS
BY NANKING GOVT.
Subject Of Considerable
Controversy Through-
out Germany To-day
ARMAMENT FACTORIES'
POLICY ATTACKED
BERLIN, Aug. 26.—The seizure
by the Nanking Government of
German steamers carrying arms
and ammunition is becoming a
subject of considerable contro-
versy throughout the country.
The newspaper "Vorwaerts" is
taking up the matter vigorously
and to-day demands that a law
should be passed forbidding Ger-
man shipping companies from
transporting arms.
It soundly attacks the policy of
the armament factories and de-
clares that they are pocketing huge
profits from these cargoes, while
the odium attached to the business
falls on the German people gen-
erally.
On the other hand, it is pointed
out in some quarters that the law
forbidding the import of arms into
China has been reached, and that
the owners of German vessels can-
not, therefore, be blamed for ship-
ping arms to the Far East. At
the same time, it is admitted that
the Berlin Government previously
tried to induce the shipping com-
pany to re-direct their steamers
when it was first intimated that
there might be trouble with China.
The "Vorwaerts" also takes an
original line in discussing the
question of the boycott of German
goods by the Cantonese authorities.
The German Government is enter-
ing a strong protest against the
boycott, but the "Vorwaerts" sug-
gests that the ill-feeling of Canton
against the Germans might have
been expected.
The participation by former
German military officers in the
civil wars in China is regarded by
the paper as the origin of the
boycott and it advocates measures
to prevent any further military
assistance being given by German
nationals to either one side or the
other.—Reuter.

军火工厂政策
受抨击
柏林，8月26日.—南京政府扣押运载武器和弹药的德国轮船一事，正成为德国全国上下极具争议的话题。《前进报》（Vorwaerts）积极介入此事，并于今日要求通过一项法律，禁止德国航运公司运输武器。
该报严厉抨击军火工厂的政策，宣称它们从这些货物中攫取巨额利润，而由此产生的恶名却由全体德国人承担。
另一方面，也有人指出，禁止向中国进口武器的法律期限已满，因此不能责怪德国船主将武器运往远东。同时，人们也承认，柏林政府此前曾试图促使航运公司在首次获悉可能与中国发生麻烦时改变轮船航线。
《前进报》在讨论广东当局抵制德货问题时也采取了独特的立场。德国政府正在对抵制行动提出强烈抗议，但《前进报》暗示，广东对德国的反感是可以预见的。
该报认为，前德国军官参与中国内战是抵制行动的根源，并主张采取措施，防止德国国民再向任何一方提供进一步的军事援助。—路透社。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, AUGUST 27, 1931

Berlin Takes
Its Stand On
Arms Seizure
Protection Denied To
Owners Of Vessel
Seized Here
NOT MADE IN GERMANY
Boycott By Canton Unjust,
Reich Remonstrates
In A Statement

BERLIN, Aug. 26.—The attitude of the German Government on the question of the seizure of war material aboard a German vessel in Shanghai, and its repercussions in the South, was defined to-day in a semi-official statement. The statement declares that the whole regrettable affair arises out of the fact that special legislation to prevent German bottoms being used for arms and ammunition shipments, enacted in 1928 for the period of 18 months, was allowed to lapse at its expiration.

At that time, the situation in China seemed to offer guarantees against the repetition of the incidents which had made special measures necessary. Thus, the law lapsed, but in the meantime shipping companies were requested to ignore all requests for the transport of war material to China.

In the present case, the Government continues, the owners of the seized vessel appealed to the Foreign Office for protection, but this was refused, it being pointed out to them that they had acted contrary to the repeated warnings given by the Government.

Finally, as regards the situation in the South, the statement declares that the German Foreign Office remonstrated with the Canton authorities, pointing out the injustice of a boycott against all German firms because of the action of one firm, and also drew attention to the fact that the shipments of arms and ammunition from other countries to Nanking were quite notorious, and that there were military and naval advisers of many nations in assisting against the Cantonese.

Finally, the statement vigorously denies the report that German firms are supplying arms to the Nanking Government, declaring that such reports are absolutely without foundation in fact.

《字林西报》，1931年8月27日，星期四

柏林就
武器查扣
表明立场
在此被查扣
船只船主
 denied 保护
非德国制造
广东抵制不公，
德国外交部
在声明中提出抗议

柏林，8月26日.—德国政府就上海一艘德国船只上战争物资被查扣一事及其在南方引发的反响的态度，今日在一项半官方声明中予以明确。声明称，整个令人遗憾的事件源于这样的事实：为防止德国船只被用于运输武器和弹药而于1928年颁布、有效期为18个月的特别立法，在到期后被允许失效。

当时，中国的局势似乎提供了保证，防止那些曾使特别措施成为必要的事件重演。因此，该法律失效，但与此同时，航运公司被要求无视所有将战争物资运往中国的请求。

声明继续称，在目前的情况下，被查扣船只的船主曾向外交部寻求保护，但遭到拒绝，并向他们指出，他们的行为违背了政府反复发出的警告。

最后，关于南方的局势，声明称德国外交部已向广东当局提出抗议，指出因一家公司的行为而对所有德国公司实行抵制是不公正的，并提请注意其他国家向南京运送武器和弹药已是众所周知的事实，且有许多国家的军事和海军顾问在协助对抗广东方面。

最后，声明坚决否认德国公司向南京政府供应武器的报道，宣称此类报道完全毫无事实根据。

Disposal Of Arms
Cargo Of German
Vessel Undecided

$2,000,000 In Ammunition

ship carrying a cargo of tons of ex-
plosives as well as a yet undeter-

德国船只

THE CHINA PRESS, TUESDAY, AUGUST 25, 1931
2177

Second Arms Cargo
For Canton Captured

Steamer Bonus Escorted Into Harbor By Customs
Cruiser With Enough Ammunition To Wipe
Out An Army; Junkers Planes Are Confiscated

Another floating arsenal, the
Bonus, second vessel of the German
Rickmers Line laden with tons of
arms, ammunition, and explosives to
come to Shanghai within three days,
entered the harbor yesterday.
As in the case of the first ship,
the R. C. Rickmers, arms and am-
munition estimated in greater
quantities than those of the first
ship, were seized by the national
government, after the ship had been
escorted into Woosung from the 12-
mile-limit of Chinese jurisdiction by
the customs cruiser, heavily armored
customs launch and as many river
police as could be mustered from
everyday duties.

Were For Canton
As reported exclusively in the
China Press on Sunday and Mon-
day, the arms were originally con-
signed to Cantonese factions. Nan-
king officials were said to have
learned of the shipments and order-
ed delivery of the arms direct to
Shanghai under penalty of boycott
from Chinese ports. For this rea-
son the ships avoided Cantonese
waters, and came direct to Shang-
hai with their cargoes.
Yesterday's check of cargo of the
R. C. Rickmers revealed appalling
quantities of arms, ammunition
and explosives.

Planes Seized
Three late model Junkers pursuit
planes, 600 machine guns, hundreds
of cases of ammunition, hundreds
of Mauser revolvers, rifles, and
other firearms were numbered
among the seized fighting equip-
ment.
At the Rickmers Line agency at
451 Kiangse Road cargo manifests
lists showed among other items
astounding amounts of explosives
brought into port by the R. C.
Rickmers. Among them were:
Big T. N. T. Shipment
Smokeless Powder 53,200 kgs.
T. N. T. 25,200 „
Dynamite 73,500 lbs.
Detonators 2,010 „
Fetonators 5,925 „
Gelignite 1,365 kgs.
Dynamite 5,460 „
Detonators 225 „
Smokeless Powder 67 „
Blast Gelatine 3,870 lbs.
Friction Tubes 680 „
Detonators 127 „
Blast Gelatine 1,245 „
All these goods was taken off the
ship at Woosung by registered
lighters under instructions from
customs authorities. It is expected
that the Bonus cargo will be identi-
cal with this but in larger quanti-
ties.
In a statement to the China Press
yesterday, Captain D. Harff, mas-
ter of the R. C. Rickmers, denied
complicity of either himself or his
line in Chinese politics.

Dislikes Press
"I am merely the captain of my
ship," Capt. Harff declared. "My
company's business is transportation
of goods of any legal nature from
one port to another. I conducted
this cargo as I should do any
other."
Captain Harff did not look fa-
vorably on the visit from a mem-
ber of the press. "On a former
trip to Shanghai, papers reported
me as involved with a $1,000,000
shipment of opium. My reputation
was almost ruined," the master said.
He declared himself as innocent
with the charges of the press on
that occasion as during the present
instance.

Describes Seizure
Captain Harff obligingly describ-
ed the seizure of arms for the China
Press representative.
"I was on the bridge as we came
into Chinese waters," the shipping
man narrated. "Without warning
a Chinese customs cruiser approach-
ed and flashed its lights on the
name of the ship. We asked what
they wanted, and the officials of the
cruiser demanded that we stop and
drop anchor.
"This, the pilot objected to," con-
tinued the master. "We shouted
back that we were directly over a
cable and that dropping anchor in
this spot would be exceedingly dan-
gerous, but nevertheless commands
to drop anchor were repeated and
we obeyed. A gun was fired.

Marines Take Charge
"Without further ado, the cus-
toms craft drew alongside, and
seven marines armed to the teeth
leaped over the side and ordered us
to proceed cautiously to Woosung,
which we did. The invaders made
a check of the nature and quantity
of our cargo. When we arrived at
Woosung the arms, ammunition,
and explosives were seized and
stored in the government arsenal at
Lay Road."
The captain said that while at
Manila he was ordered by cabled
instructions from line officials in
Hamburg to proceed directly to
Shanghai and not to enter Southern
Chinese waters.

Feared Capture
"At many ports I heard indirect-
ly that Chinese consuls had been
warned to watch the progress of
the R. C. Rickmers. When I re-
ceived word in Manila to come
direct to Shanghai, I reasoned that
company officials were afraid that in
the event of our entering Chinese
